newsitem.title: UK: Training levy to increase SA port charges warning.
newsitem.headline: Training levy to increase SA port charges warning.

text.p: A South African shipping agent has warned that the cost of handling cargo at the country's ports will rise as a result of a government decision to levy industries to fund training.
Rennies Ship Agency said in a statement: "Shipowners will be called upon to make a significant ongoing contribution to staff training needs in South Africa."
Two surcharges are to be introduced with the creation of a Maritime Industry Training Board (MITB), the company said.
Rennies said a 0.5 percent surcharge on invoices would be applicable to all vessels calling at South African ports to handle cargo.
It added that legislation would also require training stamps to be bought from the MITB and affixed to all outward clearance documents.
The cost of the stamps, which are expected to come into use this June, will range from rand 100 to rand 900 depending on vessel gross tonnage.

Rennies added that the Association of Ship Agents and Brokers of South Africa was seeking legal advice about the validity of the marine sector levy on the basis that foreign shipowners were being asked to finance the training needs of South African companies.
